name: ingredient_vs_product
description: Ingredient concept (IN) versus a specific clinical drug (SCD) containing it
failure_mode_supported: An ingredient-level fact treated as evidence about one specific strength/dose form (or vice versa)
does_not_establish: Does not show which product a patient actually takes; does not show the evidence is correct

name: single_vs_combination
description: Single-ingredient product versus a multi-ingredient product that contains it
failure_mode_supported: Evidence about a single agent attributed to its combination product (or the reverse)
does_not_establish: Does not show the clinical statement is wrong, only that the two targets are distinct concepts

name: strength_variants_same_combination
description: Two SCDs with the same ingredients and dose form but different strengths
failure_mode_supported: Strength-specific evidence attributed to the wrong strength variant of the same combination
does_not_establish: Does not model titration, dosing schedule, or clinical appropriateness of a strength

name: strength_variants_single_ingredient
description: Two SCDs with the same single ingredient/dose form but different strengths
does_not_establish: Same as C3; only two variants per ingredient are sampled, not all

name: dose_form_variants
description: Same ingredient with different dose form (immediate vs extended release)
failure_mode_supported: Evidence for one release profile attributed to another
does_not_establish: Does not encode pharmacokinetics or interchangeability

name: salt_form_precise_ingredient
description: Precise ingredients (PIN) that share one base ingredient (IN)
failure_mode_supported: Treating salt forms as identical, or as different drugs, without the verifier knowing which
does_not_establish: Whether salt forms are clinically interchangeable is not represented in RxNorm

name: distinct_medication_wrong_target
description: Two ingredients/products with no shared ingredient and look-alike names
failure_mode_supported: Evidence about drug A attributed to drug B after a later-turn target switch
does_not_establish: RxNorm shows distinctness only; turn structure and the attribution error come from other data

name: shared_ingredient_different_partner
description: Products/combinations sharing exactly one ingredient, or a combination versus its component
failure_mode_supported: Partial-overlap confusion, e.g. evidence for one combination attributed to another sharing an ingredient
does_not_establish: Overlap is detected structurally; clinical relevance of the overlap is not represented

name: brand_vs_generic
description: Branded drug (SBD) versus its generic counterpart (SCD) via tradename_of
failure_mode_supported: Brand/generic identity handling; same ingredients and strength but different concepts
does_not_establish: Does not establish label equivalence or that a DailyMed label corresponds to the concept

name: underspecified_or_nonmatching_input
description: Input strings that match no RxNorm normalized string under exact casefold/whitespace matching (non-RxNorm wording, non-RxNorm ingredient order, missing salt or dose form)
failure_mode_supported: Forced matching of an underspecified or differently-worded medication mention
does_not_establish: Exact string matching only; not a measure of how a real linking system behaves. No string in this subset maps to more than one RXCUI, so multi-concept string ambiguity is not represented

name: ingredient_level_mention_fanout
description: A valid ingredient (IN) or multiple-ingredient (MIN) concept that is contained in many candidate SCD products
failure_mode_supported: Treating an ingredient-level mention as sufficient to identify one specific product (strength/dose form)
does_not_establish: Fan-out is counted over the Current Prescribable Content subset only; it is not a count of all products ever marketed
